\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بڑبڑانا} (baṛbaṛānā)}{بڑبڑانا (baṛbaṛānā)}]{\ur{بڑبڑانا} (baṛbaṛānā) — to mutter; to grumble}

\label{lesson:UR-C463-barbarana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for innocent, then the Urdu for to be led astray.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بڑبڑانا}}
\textbf{\ur{بڑبڑانا}} — \emph{baṛbaṛānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to mutter; to grumble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادا} \ur{اکیلے} \ur{بیٹھ} \ur{کر} \ur{بڑبڑاتے} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādā akele baiṭh kar baṛbaṛāte haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather sits on his own and mutters.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{کچھ} \ur{بڑبڑایا}, \emph{voh kuchh baṛbaṛāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بڑبڑانا}} (\emph{baṛbaṛānā}) is inherited from \emph{baḍabaḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}grumble, mutter\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs and treats as an imitation of the sound (CDIAL 9122).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṛbaṛānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṛbaṛānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādā akele baiṭh kar baṛbaṛāte haiṅ.} — My grandfather sits on his own and mutters.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for innocent, then the Urdu for to be led astray, then say \emph{baṛbaṛānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بڑبڑانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To mutter; to grumble\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گپ} (gap)}{گپ (gap)}]{\ur{گپ} (gap) — idle chat}

\label{lesson:UR-C463-gap}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to be led astray, then the Urdu for to mutter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گپ}}
\textbf{\ur{گپ}} — \emph{gap} — \textquotedblleft{}idle chat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{چائے} \ur{پر} \ur{دوستوں} \ur{کی} \ur{گپ} \ur{دیر} \ur{تک} \ur{چلی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chāy par dostoṅ kī gap der tak chalī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Over tea the friends chatted for a long time.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گپ}} (\emph{gap}) is inherited from \emph{gappa}, \textquotedblleft{}tittle-tattle\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 4022).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gap}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gap}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chāy par dostoṅ kī gap der tak chalī.} — Over tea the friends chatted for a long time.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to be led astray, then the Urdu for to mutter, then say \emph{gap} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to mutter, then the Urdu for idle chat.

\begin{quote}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سرگوشی} \ur{کرنا} (sargoshī karnā)}{سرگوشی کرنا (sargoshī karnā)}]{\ur{سرگوشی} \ur{کرنا} (sargoshī karnā) — to whisper}

\label{lesson:UR-C463-sargoshi-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for idle chat, then the Urdu for hushed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سرگوشی} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سرگوشی} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{sargoshī karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to whisper\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دونوں} \ur{سہیلیاں} \ur{کلاس} \ur{میں} \ur{سرگوشی} \ur{کر} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{donoṅ saheliyāṅ klās meṅ sargoshī kar rahī thīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The two friends were whispering in class.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کان} \ur{میں} \ur{سرگوشی} \ur{کی}, \emph{us ne kān meṅ sargoshī kī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سرگوشی} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{sargoshī karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{سرگوشی}}, usually traced to Persian \emph{sargōshī}, \textquotedblleft{}a whisper\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{sar}, \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{gōsh}, \textquotedblleft{}ear\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sargoshī karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{donoṅ saheliyāṅ klās meṅ sargoshī kar rahī thīṅ.} — The two friends were whispering in class.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for idle chat, then the Urdu for hushed, then say \emph{sargoshī karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گنگ} (gung)}{گنگ (gung)}]{\ur{گنگ} (gung) — speechless; struck dumb}

\label{lesson:UR-C463-gung}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for hushed, then the Urdu for to whisper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گنگ}}
\textbf{\ur{گنگ}} — \emph{gung} — \textquotedblleft{}speechless; struck dumb\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{خبر} \ur{سن} \ur{کر} \ur{وہ} \ur{گنگ} \ur{رہ} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khabar sun kar voh gung rah gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He was struck dumb when he heard the news.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گنگ}} (\emph{gung}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{gung}, \textquotedblleft{}mute\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gung}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gung}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khabar sun kar voh gung rah gayā.} — He was struck dumb when he heard the news.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for hushed, then the Urdu for to whisper, then say \emph{gung} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Kind and Cruel to Talkers and Quiet Ones}

\label{lesson:UR-R463-review-456-463}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for cruel and hard-hearted.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item cruel, hard-hearted, a kindness done, grace, cruelty
  \item sincere, crafty, to believe someone, integrity, a promise
  \item to be patient, forbearance, to put up with, to snap at, to bear
  \item bountiful, selfish, open-handed, miserly, alms
  \item bold, daring, a risk, to fight, valiant
  \item consideration, courteous, refinement, moral conduct, to show respect
  \item wits, wise, naive, innocent, to be led astray
  \item to mutter, idle chat, hushed, to whisper, speechless
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Cruel? (\textbf{\ur{ظالم}}, \emph{zālim}.) Hard-hearted? (\textbf{\ur{سنگدل}}, \emph{sangdil}.) A kindness done? (\textbf{\ur{احسان}}, \emph{ehsān}.) Grace? (\textbf{\ur{کرم}}, \emph{karam}.) Cruelty? (\textbf{\ur{ستم}}, \emph{sitam}.) Sincere? (\textbf{\ur{مخلص}}, \emph{mukhlis}.) Crafty? (\textbf{\ur{مکار}}, \emph{makkār}.) To believe someone? (\textbf{\ur{اعتبار} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{etibār karnā}.) Integrity? (\textbf{\ur{دیانت}}, \emph{diyānat}.) A promise? (\textbf{\ur{وعدہ}}, \emph{vādā}.) To be patient? (\textbf{\ur{صبر} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{sabr karnā}.) Forbearance? (\textbf{\ur{تحمل}}, \emph{tahammul}.) To put up with? (\textbf{\ur{برداشت} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{bardāsht karnā}.) To snap at? (\textbf{\ur{جھڑکنا}}, \emph{jhiṛaknā}.) To bear? (\textbf{\ur{سہنا}}, \emph{sahnā}.) Bountiful? (\textbf{\ur{فیاض}}, \emph{fayyāz}.) Selfish? (\textbf{\ur{خود} \ur{غرض}}, \emph{khud gharaz}.) Open-handed? (\textbf{\ur{سخی}}, \emph{sakhī}.) Miserly? (\textbf{\ur{بخیل}}, \emph{bakhīl}.) Alms? (\textbf{\ur{صدقہ}}, \emph{sadqā}.) Bold? (\textbf{\ur{دلیر}}, \emph{diler}.) Daring? (\textbf{\ur{جانباز}}, \emph{jānbāz}.) A risk? (\textbf{\ur{جوکھم}}, \emph{jokham}.) To fight? (\textbf{\ur{لڑنا}}, \emph{laṛnā}.) Valiant? (\textbf{\ur{دلاور}}, \emph{dilāvar}.) Consideration? (\textbf{\ur{لحاظ}}, \emph{lihāz}.) Courteous? (\textbf{\ur{شائستہ}}, \emph{shāistā}.) Refinement? (\textbf{\ur{تہذیب}}, \emph{tahzīb}.) Moral conduct? (\textbf{\ur{اخلاق}}, \emph{akhlāq}.) To show respect? (\textbf{\ur{احترام} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{ehtirām karnā}.) Wits? (\textbf{\ur{عقل}}, \emph{aql}.) Wise? (\textbf{\ur{دانا}}, \emph{dānā}.) Naive? (\textbf{\ur{نادان}}, \emph{nādān}.) Innocent? (\textbf{\ur{معصوم}}, \emph{māsūm}.) To be led astray? (\textbf{\ur{بہکنا}}, \emph{bahaknā}.) To mutter? (\textbf{\ur{بڑبڑانا}}, \emph{baṛbaṛānā}.) Idle chat? (\textbf{\ur{گپ}}, \emph{gap}.) Hushed? (\textbf{\ur{چپ}}, \emph{chup}.) To whisper? (\textbf{\ur{سرگوشی} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{sargoshī karnā}.) Speechless? (\textbf{\ur{گنگ}}, \emph{gung}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
